According to reports, Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, indicating that this cooling technology will play a more important role in its future hardware product lineup. Details are as follows.

Apple is betting bigger on vapor chamber cooling technology

Weibo leak account "定焦數碼" posted that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber orders," and speculated that this move is "likely to prepare stronger cooling solutions for its first foldable iPhone and next year's anniversary edition models."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, and this change successfully resolved the overheating issues that had persisted over the past few generations.

Vapor chambers work by evaporating a small amount of liquid near a heat source, then condensing it at a cooler location, dissipating the heat over a larger area before letting the liquid flow back to repeat the cycle.

To see the entire process in action, you can watch this excellent video from Know Art:

Although the Weibo post speculates that Apple's increased procurement this time is in preparation for the iPhone Ultra and the rumored anniversary edition iPhone launching in 2027, looking back at the timeline, it would be more reasonable for this year's product lineup to adopt this technology first.

Apple is reportedly asking suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, an increase from the previous target of 7 to 8 million. Meanwhile, the company has also stockpiled about 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

In addition to the increased orders, there are also reports that Apple has resolved previous hinge and yield issues, clearing obstacles to ramping up production ahead of the September launch.
